intro: On TikTok, people decide in a moment whether to watch or swipe, so your product needs to show up right away and look like it belongs in the feed. AIVideosUGC turns one product photo and a short description into a vertical video ad of 6, 10 or 15 seconds. You might describe a hand lifting the product off a desk, a bottle on a gym bench, or a phone case catching the light, and the clip is built around that moment.

It suits sellers trying their first TikTok ad and marketers who need a new angle every week without booking a shoot. Each video is made one at a time, with the credit cost shown before you start. Want a different opening? Run another version. Once you download the file, add captions, a sound and your offer in TikTok or CapCut, then upload it to TikTok Ads Manager.
tips: Get the product on screen in the very first second, before anyone has a reason to swipe.
Keep the product clear of the right edge and the bottom of the frame, where TikTok's buttons and caption sit.
Swap in a fresh version once an ad starts to feel familiar, because the same clip wears out quickly in a fast feed.

ideas.d: Describe a hand turning the product toward the camera so the clip feels like something a shopper filmed at home.

ideas.t: Use it in the first frame
ideas.d: Open on the product doing its job, like a lint roller clearing a sweater or a mug steaming on a desk, so nobody wonders what it is.
Make separate versions that start on the box, the product in hand and the product in use, then see which one holds attention in Ads Manager.

faq.q: Can I send the video straight to TikTok from AIVideosUGC?
faq.a: No. Download the file, then upload it in TikTok Ads Manager or the TikTok app. That's also where you can add captions and pick a sound.

faq.q: How long should my TikTok ad be?
faq.a: There's no single right length. Six seconds suits one striking shot, while 15 seconds leaves room to show the product being used. Try more than one and compare.

faq.q: Does the video come with music?
faq.a: We don't add music, so choose a sound in TikTok or CapCut before you post.

faq.q: Do I need to label an AI-generated ad on TikTok?
faq.a: TikTok has its own rules for AI-generated content, and they get updated. Check the current guidance in your account when you upload, and turn on the label if it applies.
